html:
The Pericú were an Indigenous people of the Cape Region, the southern tip of Baja California in Mexico, and of nearby islands. They spoke a language that is barely recorded and died out by about 1800.

They lived by fishing, collecting shellfish and gathering wild plants, and used rafts to reach the islands. Some scholars think their long, narrow skulls point to an early migration separate from other Native Americans, though this is debated. Their neighbours to the north were the Guaycura and the Monqui.

Ships of the Manila galleons passed their coast, and in 1587 the English raider Thomas Cavendish captured a galleon off Cape San Lucas. Jesuit missions came in the 1720s. The Pericú rose against them in 1734, but disease and war destroyed them within decades.
sum: The Pericú were an Indigenous people of the Cape Region, the southern tip of Baja California in Mexico, and of nearby islands. They spoke a language that is barely recorded and died out by about 1800.
